intuition: Testing many examples is like checking many steps on a staircase: it does not tell you how every possible staircase behaves.
learningGoal: Algorithm discovery, computational complexity, and the difference between empirical speedups and mathematical proof.
exerciseNote: CPU-only: run the packaged SAT baseline and explain what its tests can and cannot establish.

quiz.question: Explain why testing a proposed algorithm on one million SAT instances cannot, by itself, establish its worst-case complexity for all possible inputs.
quiz.explanation: A finite test set checks particular instances. A worst-case complexity claim quantifies over all permitted inputs and sizes, so it needs a rigorous argument under a precise computational model.
